summary: In a US copyright case brought by music publishers Universal Music Group, Concord and ABKCO, Anthropic expert Olivia Chen submitted a declaration on how often Claude might reproduce song lyrics. A footnote cited an American Statistician article in support of her rare-event sampling discussion. At a 13 May 2025 hearing, the publishers’ lawyer Matt Oppenheim challenged the title and authors as belonging to an article that did not exist, and Magistrate Judge Susan van Keulen ordered Anthropic to explain. In a 15 May declaration, Anthropic lawyer Ivana Dukanovic said a Latham & Watkins colleague had found a real article, then she asked Claude to format its citation using the correct link. Claude returned the right journal, year and link but the wrong title and authors; the legal team reviewed the article and corrected volume and page numbers yet missed those errors and two other wording errors. On 23 May, Judge van Keulen found the citation issue serious, noted that the applicable standing order required lead trial counsel to certify personal verification of content accuracy and that neither the certification nor that verification had occurred, struck paragraph 9 of Chen’s declaration, and said the issue undermined the declaration’s overall credibility.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy re-adjudication retains VIGIL-FC-000062 Epistemic Reliance Calibration and adds VIGIL-FC-000016 Required Verification Completion as an independently evidenced secondary failure. FC-000062 applies because false title and author metadata generated during Claude citation formatting entered a court-facing expert declaration below the source-fidelity threshold required for formal legal reliance. FC-000016 applies because the May 23 court order identifies a specific standing-order requirement that lead trial counsel certify personal verification of content accuracy and expressly states that neither the certification nor verification occurred. The narrower manual cite-check described by Dukanovic does not substitute for that required verification. The court struck paragraph 9 and recorded a credibility consequence. Early allegations of a wholly nonexistent underlying article remain superseded by the filed declaration and order confirming that the real article existed and was correctly linked.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Reuters records the 13 May hearing, Matt Oppenheim’s challenge and Judge Susan van Keulen’s order for an explanation. Dukanovic’s filed 15 May declaration supplies the source chain: a Latham & Watkins associate found the real McGrath and Burke article; Chen relied on it for rare-event sampling; Dukanovic provided its correct link to Claude for a formatted legal citation; and Claude returned the correct journal, year and link but incorrect authors and title. Dukanovic says the team reviewed the article and corrected volume and page numbers yet missed those errors and two other wording errors. Judge van Keulen’s 23 May order then independently characterised the issue as serious, stated that Judge Lee’s standing order required lead trial counsel to certify that counsel had personally verified content accuracy, found that neither the certification nor that verification had occurred, struck paragraph 9 of Chen’s declaration, and recorded that the issue undermined the overall credibility of Chen’s written declaration. The order also confirmed that the underlying article existed and had been properly linked, narrowing the occurrence from a wholly fictitious source to false citation metadata plus a distinct required-verification failure. The preserved record does not establish a monetary sanction, a merits judgment caused by the citation, or a broader deprivation of a party’s legal rights.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The directly reviewed declaration and later court order support a compound current-taxonomy assessment. Epistemic Reliance Calibration captures the inaccurate Claude-formatted citation being incorporated into a court-facing expert declaration despite insufficient source fidelity for that reliance context. Required Verification Completion is independently supported by the court’s finding that the applicable standing order required lead trial counsel to certify personal verification of content accuracy and that neither the certification nor that verification had occurred. The legal team’s narrower manual cite-check does not defeat that mapping because it was not the required verification identified by the court. The court struck paragraph 9 and recorded a credibility consequence, but the preserved evidence does not establish a monetary sanction or broader merits deprivation attributable to the citation error.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence demonstrates two distinct governance boundaries. First, generated bibliographic detail was promoted into a formal legal artefact below the source-fidelity threshold required for court-facing reliance. Second, the court identified a specific standing-order verification and certification requirement that had not been completed, even though the legal team had performed a narrower cite-check. A performed but incomplete checking activity therefore must not be treated as equivalent to completion of the verification posture actually required by the governing process.
